jobs.description:
Lifecycle Marketing Manager

Remote (minimum 4-hour overlap with US Eastern hours) | Marketing | Reports to: Director, Revenue Marketing

Time Doctor is hiring a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to own the marketing-led customer journey from the moment an account starts paying. You will decide who hears what, when, based on which behaviour, and toward which commercial outcome. Your job is to turn customer behaviour and usage signals into adoption, retention, expansion and reactivation revenue, and to run that engine AI-first, building agents and agentic workflows that do real work.

Who we are

Time Doctor is a workforce analytics platform that gives distributed teams the visibility they need to improve trust and performance. We serve remote, hybrid and outsourced organisations worldwide, with particular strength in BPO, healthcare and tech services. We are bootstrapped, profitable and fully remote, with team members across 30+ countries. We built a durable business on customer revenue rather than venture capital, and we are now focused on growing it.

The role

You will own the lifecycle marketing program for our paying customers: the 30/60/90 onboarding plays, ongoing customer communications, customer segmentation, and the expansion and retention plays that grow and keep the base. You design the journeys, brief the work, QA it and measure it, and you own the revenue outcome.

Three things define this seat.

  • The number. Your primary measure is the qualified expansion and cross-sell opportunities Lifecycle generates and surfaces. Expansion revenue, net revenue retention and at-risk recovery sit right behind it, shared with CS, Sales and Product.

  • The lane. You own orchestration and outcomes across the customer base, not every surface you touch. PMM owns the message, GTM Ops builds the scoring and routing, and Growth and CS co-define the signals with you. You make it all work together.

  • The operating model. This is an AI-first role, and AI fluency is the job. The bar is that you can stand up an agent that does real work, not describe one. Accelerating Time Doctor's AI-first operating model is an explicit expectation of the seat.

This is a systems role. You build repeatable, automated journeys rather than one-off campaigns, and you keep human ownership of segmentation logic, offer design, guardrails, final QA and the commercial call.

Who you are

  • You treat a revenue number as yours, and you design every journey toward adoption, retention or expansion.

  • You have high agency. When a journey underperforms, you find out why and fix it.

  • You are commercially minded. You turn customer signals into revenue.

  • You are analytical and cohort-fluent. You read behaviour and act on where customers stall or grow.

  • You think in systems. You would rather build a repeatable, automated flow than run another one-off campaign.

  • You work cleanly across Growth, CS, PMM and GTM Ops without needing to own their surfaces, and you turn ambiguous boundaries into working agreements.

  • You build with AI. Agents and agentic workflows are how you get work done.

What you will own

  • Onboarding and adoption. The marketing-led 30/60/90 program that gets new paying customers to first value, plus ongoing adoption of key capabilities and education, including driving traffic to TD Academy and running education webinars end to end. You own the day-0 handoff: the trigger and the data that enrol a new customer in the right journey.

  • Segmentation and journey orchestration. Segmenting paying customers on profile, product usage, engagement, lifecycle stage, adoption state, expansion propensity and churn risk, then designing, building and QA-ing the journeys and triggers on top, so the right cohort gets the right play at the right moment.

  • Expansion and cross-sell. Plays that grow existing accounts through seats, add-ons and cross-sell. You co-define expansion signals with Growth and CS, turn them into segments and plays, and route qualified opportunities to Sales and CS, with GTM Ops implementing detection and actions.

  • Retention and win-back. Proactive plays against at-risk cohorts, air cover for CS retention efforts, re-engagement of dormant accounts, and win-back of churned accounts where it is commercially worthwhile.

  • Renewal-moment marketing. Value-recap and air-cover campaigns timed to the renewal window, reinforcing realised value ahead of the CS conversation.

  • Customer communications. Audience, segmentation, timing and orchestration for the customer newsletter, customer webinars, feature and release comms, and lifecycle-triggered in-app announcements. PMM owns the message. You own distribution.

  • Advocacy and review sites. Identifying advocates and triggering review, referral, testimonial and reference asks at the right lifecycle moment, including activating the promoters CS surfaces through NPS. You fully own review-site management and take the case studies Content and PMM produce to market.

  • Lifecycle analytics and experimentation. Performance across every journey, from onboarding completion and time-to-value through to expansion, retention, renewal support and win-back. You find where customers stall, drop off, expand or disengage, and you keep improving the programs.

  • AI in the workflow. Agentic workflows for segmentation, usage and account signal interpretation, journey and trigger build and testing, customer comms drafting and variants, propensity and churn scoring drafts, cohort analysis and drop-off detection. You decide what runs autonomously, what needs human judgement, and how each workflow gets operationalised with GTM Ops.

This role may not suit you if

  • You measure yourself on sends, opens and campaign volume rather than on revenue adopted, kept and grown.

  • You prefer launching one-off campaigns to building journeys that run on their own.

  • AI for you means prompt libraries and screenshots. We need someone who has built agents that do real work.

  • Your experience is mostly top-of-funnel. This role starts the moment an account becomes a paying customer.

  • You need to own every surface you touch. PMM owns the message and GTM Ops builds the scoring and routing, and this seat depends on working well with both.

  • You cannot commit to at least four hours a day of overlap with US Eastern business hours.

What a realistic week looks like

A cohort review showing where last month's new customers stalled before day 30, and a fix to the onboarding journey that ships the same week. A working session with CS on an at-risk cohort and the play you will run against it. Two expansion opportunities your signals surfaced, qualified and routed to Sales. An agent you built to draft and QA journey variants, tightened after its first run. A value-recap campaign going out to accounts entering their renewal window. Live collaboration during US Eastern hours, async for the rest of the day.

Requirements

Your experience

  • 5 to 7 years in lifecycle, CRM, customer or retention marketing at a B2B SaaS company.

  • A track record of designing and running behaviour-triggered customer journeys, with adoption, retention or expansion outcomes you owned. You know your numbers and can walk us through them.

  • Comfortable working from product-usage and account data to define segments, propensity and churn logic. You can specify the scoring and routing, even though GTM Ops builds it.

  • Fluent in a marketing automation or lifecycle stack such as HubSpot, and in cohort analysis.

  • Experience running expansion, cross-sell or renewal-support programs, and coordinating opportunity handoff with CS and Sales.

  • A clear understanding of where lifecycle ends and Growth and CS begin, and the ability to work cleanly across those lines.

  • Hands-on experience building agents or agentic workflows that do real work. You can show us what you built and what it does.

  • Remote, with a minimum four-hour daily overlap with US Eastern (ET) business hours.

Nice to have

  • Product-led SaaS experience.

  • More than four hours of daily overlap with US Eastern business hours.

  • Background in workforce analytics, time tracking, HR tech or productivity software.

  • Experience marketing to BPO, outsourcing, healthcare or tech services customers.

The team you are joining

You will report to our Director, Revenue Marketing. You will work closely with Growth and CS on expansion and churn signals, with PMM and Content on messaging and proof assets, with GTM Ops on scoring, routing and journey implementation, and with Sales and CS on the opportunities you hand forward.

How we will measure success

  • Qualified expansion and cross-sell opportunities you generate and surface. This is the headline measure and the one you control most directly.

  • Expansion revenue, net revenue retention contribution and at-risk recovery, which CS, Sales and Product also influence.

  • Onboarding completion, time-to-value and product adoption depth among paying customers, as the leading indicators.

  • Advocacy volume across reviews, referrals and references, renewal-support coverage, and revenue recovered through win-back.

Your first 90 days

  • Days 1 to 30. Map the post-conversion journey and where customers stall. Audit the current 30/60/90 onboarding and customer comms. Document the conversion handoff: the trigger and the data that must travel with a new customer. Agree the first expansion and churn signals with Growth and CS, and baseline adoption, retention and expansion.

  • Days 31 to 60. Launch or repair the 30/60/90 onboarding. Stand up the first expansion play and one renewal-moment campaign. Set up cohort reporting, introduce AI-assisted segmentation and comms, and get review-site management and one advocacy trigger (NPS promoters from CS) live.

  • Days 61 to 90. Scale the expansion and retention plays that are working. Run a win-back pilot. Establish expansion-opportunity routing to Sales and CS with GTM Ops, then present the adoption, retention and expansion baseline alongside a lifecycle roadmap.

Why this role

  • You own a real revenue number, from the moment a customer converts.

  • You get a clear lane. Growth, CS, PMM and GTM Ops are your partners, and your focus is orchestration and outcomes.

  • You work AI-first from day one, at a company where accelerating an AI-first operating model is an explicit expectation.

  • We are profitable and bootstrapped. Your budget comes from customers, not from a burn rate.

  • Fully remote and flexible, working with talented people in 30+ countries.

Our hiring approach

Because this is an AI-first role, our process asks you to prove it. Expect a working session where you show agents or agentic workflows you have built, then stand up or walk through one live, applied to a real customer-lifecycle problem. Prompt libraries and screenshots are not enough. We want to see how you architect, orchestrate and operationalise the work.

This is a full-time, 100% remote role. We are an equal opportunity employer and we value diversity and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status or disability.

We hire globally, and this particular role requires a minimum four-hour daily overlap with US Eastern business hours. Our Talent Attraction team will walk you through the details during your first conversation.

Learn more about us at

The Patient Access Appeals Case Manager is responsible for supporting patients through the denial and appeal process, coordinating with healthcare providers, insurance companies, and patients to ensure seamless access to our innovative DME device. This position will play a supportive role in ensuring the successful commercialization of our product by developing and executing reimbursement strategies, establishing relationships with payers, and navigating the complex healthcare reimbursement landscape.

  • Collaborate with healthcare providers to obtain necessary documentation and clinical information for insurance claims and prior authorization requests
  • Coordinate with insurance companies to ensure timely and accurate processing of claims and prior authorization requests
  • Stay up to date with insurance policies, coverage criteria, and reimbursement guidelines to provide accurate information and assist in obtaining coverage for patients.
  • Help to identify and address any access or reimbursement challenges, working closely with cross-functional teams to develop solutions
  • Provide exceptional customer service to patients, healthcare providers, and insurance companies, addressing inquiries and resolving any access-related issues.

  • Assess incoming denials and log in the database to identify trends in denials, new medical policies, as well as successful talk tracks and language used in successful appeals
  • Continuously evaluate and enhance the commercial appeals process for efficiency and effectiveness

We're so happy you're here! Thank you for checking our job out and we hope to have the chance to meet you in our interview process!

About the role

Grüns is scaling fast, and our supply chain has to move faster than the demand. As our Supply Chain Specialist, you'll be the execution engine behind it: owning purchase orders from creation to receipt, keeping inventory and inbound data airtight, and catching risk before it ever reaches a customer. You'll work side by side with our Director of Supply Chain and directly with our suppliers, co-manufacturers, and 3PLs. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role, and the work you do will protect product availability as we grow.

This role is part of our remote HQ! We have a fully remote, high-trust work environment - and also come together on a biannual basis for amazing off-sites where we can connect IRL.

In this role, you will:

  • Own day-to-day purchase order execution, moving every PO through production, shipment, receipt, and exception resolution without dropped follow-up
  • Run the operating cadence with suppliers, co-manufacturers, and 3PLs, so every confirmation, delay, decision, and committed date has one clear owner: you
  • Maintain the source of truth for available, inbound, and at-risk inventory, so the team always knows what we have, what's coming, and what's in trouble
  • Spot shortages, production delays, material constraints, freight risk, and inventory imbalances early, and escalate with a recommended action, not just a flag
  • Build Claude-powered workflows that turn raw PO, inventory, production, and freight data into exception lists, supplier communications, meeting recaps, and decision-ready summaries
  • Standardize reporting, documentation, and recurring workflows (and write the SOPs) so the team can handle higher volume with fewer manual errors

We're looking for someone who:

  • Has 1-3 years in supply chain, operations, procurement, production planning, logistics, or inventory management, working close to the physical flow of product rather than only reporting on it
  • Has worked in or around a fast-paced CPG, food/beverage, supplements, wellness, beauty, or other physical-product business (strongly preferred)
  • Has coordinated directly with external suppliers, manufacturers, or logistics partners, whether in a full-time role or internship, and held them to deadlines across multiple workstreams at once
  • Has hands-on experience with an ERP, inventory, or order management system (NetSuite-style) and can pull and organize clean source data without help
  • Uses Claude or other AI tools daily for real operational work: writes strong prompts, builds reusable workflows, and validates outputs against source data before acting on them
  • Can point to real examples of catching a problem early and driving it to resolution

Approach to the role:

  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, without losing sight of what matters most to the business
  • Proactive: follows up before the deadline, not after something is already late
  • Comfortable in ambiguity, and builds structure where processes are still taking shape
  • Takes extreme ownership: closes loops and communicates risk early
  • Collaborative and low-ego, while still holding internal teams and external partners accountable
  • Treats AI as a force multiplier on the work, never a substitute for judgment

Compensation & Benefits:

At Grüns, we're committed to providing a competitive total compensation package—grounded in market data that considers our size, stage, industry, and location. For this role, the base salary range is between $80,000 – $85,000 plus bonus depending on experience.

A bit about us...

At Grüns, we believe that foundational nutrition should be simple and convenient for everyone. We're dedicated to bringing comprehensive and real nutrition to you through our gummies, formulated from 60 nutrient-dense and whole-food ingredients. Simply enjoy a grab-and-go snack pack of gummies daily whenever fits best in your schedule and wherever life takes you.

Like you, we were disappointed. There’s an infinite number of “nutrition” companies, all focused on what’s best for them — not what’s best for you. Hundreds of products to sell you on, low-quality ingredients, and small nutrient doses. We’ve seen it all.

So we decided it was time to fix it. No more choking on and popping pills like a pharmacy. No more clean-up and disgust from gross powders. And no more cobbling together handfuls to dozens of supplements. Grüns is comprehensive nutrition, made convenient and delicious.

What we care about...

Be the Best: We hold ourselves, our teams, and our partners to an incredibly high standard - and we raise the bar constantly. "We've never done this before" isn't an excuse here. It's an invitation.

Own It: We act like our name is on the door. That means taking complete ownership of outcomes, collaborating deeply, working through roadblocks - not around them - and never waiting for someone else to solve the problem. Great owners are great partners.

Drive Impact, Urgently: We measure impact, not effort. We work smart and hard, move fast, and use every tool at our disposal - including AI - to focus our energy where it matters most.

Compensation & Perks:

For every role, we aim to have highly competitive compensation and opportunity for impact and career growth.

Everyone at Grüns works hard, but we believe in wellness and balance too. We have super strong benefits coverage -- for you and your family, generous PTO, free Grüns, and a few more perks centered around health and well-being that we can't wait to tell you about!

Backed by 40+ peer-reviewed publications and trusted by partners including the Gates Foundation, J&J, Takeda, Pivotal Ventures, and the Clinton Health Access Initiative, Surgo is building a future where healthcare organizations don't just understand human behavior, but anticipate it — making healthcare more personal, precise, and effective for everyone.

Role Summary


We are inviting applications for a Research Fellow to join Surgo Health’s Gates Foundation (GF)-funded Family Planning initiative, a multi-country study spanning Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Nigeria (Kano, Kaduna, and Lagos states), and Pakistan (Sindh).
This fellowship is centered on manuscript production. Fellows will collaborate closely with Surgo's research team to advance a priority research question – building on analysis and framing already underway – through to a submission-ready manuscript for a peer-reviewed journal.

What you’ll achieve:

What You’ll Achieve

  • Develop and lead a manuscript around an agreed priority research question, building on existing analyses and data and conducting additional analyses as needed
  • Produce a submission-ready, publication-quality manuscript for a peer-reviewed journal
  • Translate complex survey and causal-modeling findings into insights relevant to global health policy and program design
  • Contribute to Surgo Health’s growing portfolio of family planning research and thought leadership in low- and middle-income country (LMIC) contexts

Research Focus Areas

Priority Papers


You will lead on completing the analysis that has already been started. With this, you will write the manuscript, with guidance and support from the research leads throughout.
  1. Couples-linked segmentation in Northern Nigeria (Kano and Kaduna): How do women's and their partners' own attitudes toward family planning align or diverge, and what does this mean for programs designed to shift partner-related norms? This work links directly to an active program partnership focused on norm-shifting interventions in the region.
  2. Rethinking how we measure FP intention (Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Pakistan/Sindh): Standard measures of contraceptive intention – a binary yes/no, or a 12-month time horizon – may obscure meaningful variation in fertility desire, intent strength, near-term planning, and confidence. This paper aims to describe how we have developed and tested a more multidimensional approach to measuring intent across three countries.
  3. Patterns of change in FP attitudes and behaviors over time in FP journeys (Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Nigeria [Kano and Kaduna], Pakistan [Sindh]): Using panel data collected roughly a year to two after baseline, this paper aims to characterize which women's contraceptive trajectories are "sticky", and tests which baseline predictors of conversion, intent development, and discontinuation generalize across countries versus which are context-specific.

Additional Areas of Interest

If none of the priority papers above are the right fit, the following list is intended to spark ideas rather than define the boundaries. If you have an interesting idea that isn't included here, please feel free to propose it.
  • Determinants of contraceptive intention, uptake, and method choice in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Nigeria (Kano, Kaduna, Lagos), and Pakistan (Sindh)
  • Causal inference approaches to family planning behavior (e.g., Bayesian networks, causal forests, propensity score matching, doubly robust/DoubleML methods, G-computation)
  • Segmentation-informed analysis using belief- and behavior-based segments to explain heterogeneous contraceptive outcomes
  • Comparative, cross-country analysis of family planning drivers and structural barriers
  • Subgroup and geographic vulnerability (e.g., state-level variation, rural/urban differences, adolescent and youth subpopulations)
  • Contraceptive discontinuation and continuation dynamics
  • Comparative methodology, including analysis that contextualizes findings alongside established survey instruments (e.g., DHS, PMA)

Data Available to Fellows


Fellows will work with de-identified data from Surgo's Gates Foundation-funded multi-country Family Planning study: a cross-sectional baseline survey plus a longitudinal follow-up conducted at a later point in time, across Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Nigeria, and Pakistan (Sindh).
Baseline: Women's FP Survey — Representative baseline surveys of women of reproductive age (15–49), covering fertility intentions, contraceptive use and method choice, household decision-making, perceptions and norms, health system access, and information exposure. Data was collected in 2024 to early 2025 depending on the geography. Sample sizes range from roughly 7,000 women in Senegal to around 10,000 in Côte d'Ivoire and Pakistan (Sindh), with Nigeria in between. In Nigeria, the baseline covers three states — Lagos, Kano, and Kaduna.

Baseline subset: Male Partner Interviews — In a smaller subset of baseline households, the woman's male partner also completed a companion interview, capturing his perspective on decision-making, approval, and household dynamics — enabling dyadic/couple-level analysis. Partner interviews were conducted with roughly one in ten baseline households in most countries, somewhat higher in Nigeria.

Follow-up: Longitudinal Women's Survey — A subset of baseline women who consented to re-contact were re-interviewed roughly one to two years after baseline to track changes in intentions, behavior, and access over time. This enables analysis of intention-to-behavior gaps, method continuation/discontinuation, and segment transitions. Follow-up samples range from under 2,000 women in Senegal to several thousand in Côte d'Ivoire, Nigeria (Kano and Kaduna), and Pakistan (Sindh), split between women who were contraceptive users and non-users at baseline.

Fellows will receive final sample sizes, codebooks, and documentation upon onboarding.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop and lead a research paper within agreed priority areas, either building on existing analyses and insights from the GF-funded multi-country family planning studies or developing a new research question using the available data, with additional analyses as needed.
  • Synthesize and translate existing findings and/or generate new analyses to deepen understanding of the mechanisms, risk factors, and protective factors shaping family planning behaviors and outcomes.
  • If applicable, utilize rigorous quantitative and/or causal inference methods appropriate to the research question
  • Draft and revise a manuscript for submission to a peer-reviewed journal, incorporating feedback from Surgo’s research team
  • Collaborate with Surgo’s research scientists for methodological guidance and framing

Expected Outputs

  • One submission-ready manuscript for a peer-reviewed journal (primary deliverable)
  • Clean, documented analysis code and supporting analytic materials if appropriate

Program Structure & Support


Selected Fellows will receive:
  • Access to de-identified, multi-country family planning survey data under a data use agreement
  • Codebooks and methodological documentation
  • Regular check-ins with Surgo’s research team for methodological guidance and feedback on drafts
  • Methodological and analytic support
  • Guidance on funder framing and positioning
  • Co-authorship and publication support
  • Opportunity to present progress to the broader research team
Fellows will retain academic independence while benefiting from Surgo’s translational and methodological support.
Fellows are additionally supported through a structured cadence of meetings throughout the fellowship. Regular check-ins are designed to keep work on track and give fellows direct access to Surgo researchers and leadership:

Weekly check-ins with Surgo project lead(s): Fellows will meet twice per week with their respective Surgo project lead(s). These sessions are intended to support analytic progress, troubleshoot methodological questions, and provide feedback on developing outputs. Fellows are invited to join the Surgo FP analytics team meetings. This gives fellows visibility into the broader team context and an opportunity to share work in progress with colleagues across the initiative.
Leadership exposure (optional): Fellows will have two scheduled opportunities to present findings to Hannah Kemp, Chief Strategy Officer, Client Engagement and Mokshada Jain, Vice President of Global Health. These sessions are built into the fellowship calendar and are a chance to share developing work with senior leadership. Fellows who want additional exposure can also request up to two optional meetings with Vincent Huang, Senior Director of Data Science & AI, to discuss their analytic approach and findings. These sessions are available but entirely at the fellow's discretion.

Timeline

  • Project Duration: maximum 17 weeks (~4 months)
  • Earliest start date: Oct 15, 2026
Expected main deliverables include:
  • (Week 1-2): Confirmed scope of work (Week 1–2): For papers requiring new analysis, this is an analytic plan. For papers building primarily on existing analysis or an established framing (e.g., the intent measurement paper), this is instead a confirmed research question, agreed division of remaining work between the Fellow and lead(s), and a manuscript outline.
  • (Week 6 or earlier): Preliminary results or draft findings (midpoint review)
  • (Week 12 or earlier): Draft initial manuscript for internal reviews delivered
  • (Week 16-17 or earlier): Final submission-ready manuscript delivered
Authorship
Fellows are credited as co-first-author or first author depending on their contribution. All publications and external communications will follow the agreed authorship and review process. Surgo Health retains the right to review and approve all outputs prior to external submission or distribution.
Stipend
Stipend amount: $6000
Payment is milestone-based. The stipend is distributed in four equal installments, with 25% ($1,500) awarded upon the successful completion of each milestone.

About you:

About You

  • PhD candidate, postdoctoral researcher, or early-career researcher in a relevant field (e.g., public health, demography, economics, biostatistics, epidemiology, data science)
  • Strong experience in quantitative analysis, survey data, and/or causal inference methods
  • Demonstrated ability to produce rigorous, publication-quality research
  • Experienced in family planning, reproductive health in LMIC contexts is strongly preferred
  • Experience in behavioral science and program implementation context is a plus
  • Comfort working with large-scale, multi-country survey datasets
Location: Remote friendly
Travel: None required

How to Apply


Path A — Join a Priority Paper. Apply to collaborate on one of the three papers listed under Priority Papers Open for Collaboration. In place of a general statement of interest, submit a short written response (up to 1,000 words) addressing all three of the following:
  1. Understanding: In your own words, what is the core analytic challenge this paper is trying to solve, and why does it matter? (2–3 sentences)
  2. Approach: How would you approach the methodological question below for your chosen paper? Walk through your reasoning, including tradeoffs you'd weigh.
  • Couples-linked segmentation in Northern Nigeria: How would you approach measuring alignment or divergence in paired partner responses on family planning attitudes? What would guide your definition of "alignment," and how would you handle the non-independence between partners' responses?
  • Rethinking how we measure FP intention: How would you validate that a multidimensional measure of contraceptive intention (fertility desire, intent strength, near-term planning, confidence) actually captures distinct dimensions, rather than one underlying construct measured multiple ways?
  • Longitudinal typologies of FP journeys: How would you define and empirically identify "sticky" versus "fluid" contraceptive trajectories from panel data, and how would you convince yourself the resulting typology reflects real behavioral patterns rather than measurement noise?
  1. Framing & Evidence Needed: Based on what's described above, what angle or framing would you propose for this manuscript? What evidence or additional analysis would need to emerge from the data to support that framing — and what would change your mind if it didn't?
Path B — Propose Your Own Idea. Apply with your own research question, grounded in the Additional Areas of Interest listed above (or a closely related idea). Include a short concept note (up to 1,000 words) outlining your proposed question, analytic approach, and how it would draw on the available data.

All applicants should submit:
  • CV or resume
  • Path A: the written response described above (up to 1,000 words), indicating which priority paper you're applying to. This can be a Word document or PDF file attached to your application
  • Path B: the concept note described above (up to 1,000 words). This can be a Word document or PDF file attached to your application
  • One prior peer-reviewed publication (strongly preferred), as first author or a major contributing author. If that is unavailable, submit a scientific writing sample. This can be a Word document or PDF file attached to your application
  • Contact information for two references

Benefits

What You’ll Love About Surgo

  • Fantastic, fun and collaborative colleagues; opportunity to solve tough challenges in healthcare and global health
  • Ability to be entrepreneurial, with tremendous opportunities for growth
  • Public Benefit Corporation with an impact and equity mission

Our Hiring Philosophy

We hire for passion and core competencies.

We look for problem solvers and lateral thinkers.
We love it if you have done different things with your time.
If you think you are ideal for this position, write to us even if your experience doesn’t match all the requirements listed above.

Equal Opportunity and Diversity Policy

Surgo believes a diverse, inclusive staff makes a stronger team and more impactful organization, and we are committed to building and developing this team and environment. Qualified people of all races, ethnicities, cultures, ages, sex, genders, sexual orientation, gender identities and expressions, languages, social class, marital status, religions, veteran status, and disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

jobs.description:
Senior LiveOps Developer - Mobile Games

Remote - Full Time

CrazyGames, one of the world's largest browser game platforms with over 60 million monthly active users, is doubling down on its IP portfolio. We own the games we publish, and we treat each one as a live product rather than a finished project.

We're looking for a Senior LiveOps Developer who has already done this on mobile. Someone who has taken a title through soft launch and global launch, knows which live systems need to exist before you scale UA behind a game, and can build them.

This is a hands-on development role. You'll write the code for the events, the progression systems, the offers, the economy and the remote config that keep a game growing. You'll also be the person who looks at a game's numbers and says what should ship next and why, because you've run this playbook before at a mobile publisher.

What this role is not: greenfield game development, or working through a feature backlog someone else wrote. You'll be inside existing codebases almost all of the time, on games that already have players, and you'll be the one deciding what those games need.

Key outcomes for the role

  • Within 1 month, you've onboarded to one of our live published titles, gotten comfortable in its codebase, shipped your first live update to production on web and mobile, and given us your first read on what that game's LiveOps setup is missing.

  • Within 3 months, you own the LiveOps roadmap for at least one title. You've set an update cadence, shipped a meaningful live system (event framework, progression, offers, remote config, economy tuning), and we can see the effect in retention or monetization.

  • Within 6 months, you've taken a title through the run-up to global launch. The live systems, the event calendar, the balancing and the tooling are in place before UA scales behind it, and you decided what belonged there.

  • Within 12 months, LiveOps is a repeatable system across our IP portfolio rather than something that depends on you personally. Multiple live titles run in parallel on the cadence, tooling and playbook you put in place.

On a typical day you might

  • Look at retention, session length, ARPDAU and conversion for a live title, and decide what to build next.

  • Ship a seasonal event, content drop or offer to one of our live IP games on web and mobile.

  • Build the live system behind it: event framework, remote config, A/B test, progression or economy change.

  • Dive into an unfamiliar codebase to plan how a new system slots in without breaking what's already there.

  • Tell us a game is not ready for global launch yet, and what has to exist first.

  • Design and implement a new game mode, progression system or monetization hook tailored to the genre.

  • Align with the Publishing team on the LiveOps roadmap and prioritization across titles.

  • Maintain clean Git history, write down what you did, and make sure the next update is easier than the last.

What we offer

  • Join a rapidly growing publishing team at a company with 50M+ monthly users and proven platform reach.

  • Make a real impact by directly shaping the games millions of people actually play, week after week.

  • A lot of responsibility and freedom. We hire only experts and trust them to deliver excellent results.

  • Flexible working hours and location. The results are what counts!

  • 1 to 2 team weeks per year. We pay for flights and accommodation so you can have fun with the team.

  • The opportunity to play games and claim it's work.

Requirements

You're a great fit if you

  • Have 2+ years running LiveOps on shipped mobile titles. Update cadence, events, progression, economy, offers, and the reasoning behind each of them. This is the requirement we weigh most heavily. If your experience is game development without live ownership, this is not the role.

  • Have been through a mobile soft launch and a global launch, and know what has to be in place before UA scales behind a game.

  • Bring a playbook, not just execution. You've seen how strong mobile publishers run live titles, and you can apply that here instead of waiting for someone to hand you a backlog.

  • Have 3+ years of professional game development experience with shipped titles, and are still hands-on. You build the live systems yourself rather than specifying them for someone else.

  • Read metrics as a developer, not just as a consumer of dashboards. Retention, session length, ARPDAU, conversion and cohort behaviour drive what you build next.

  • Have strong mobile game development experience (iOS and Android), and understand the differences in performance, input and UX across platforms.

  • Work with analytics, A/B testing, remote config and live tooling as part of your normal workflow, not as something a separate team owns.

  • Are comfortable with monetization and ads SDKs in a LiveOps context (events, offers, balancing).

  • Are fluent in multiple languages and ecosystems, at minimum C# and JavaScript/TypeScript, and have a solid grasp of software architecture and OOP principles.

  • Can step into an existing codebase, read it, understand it, and extend it confidently.

  • Use Git effectively in team environments and care about leaving the codebase better than you found it.

  • Are pragmatic, detail-oriented, and focused on getting high-quality updates shipped fast.

  • Are a strong team player with a true ownership mindset: you collaborate openly, take full responsibility for what you ship, and treat every game you work on as your own product to nurture and grow.

  • Are proficient in English (working language).

Nice to have

  • Web game development experience. Our platform is browser-first, so our games ship on web as well as mobile. We'd rather hire the right live experience and get you up to speed on web than compromise on the LiveOps side.

  • Multiplayer and networking experience: client/server architecture, real-time sync, matchmaking, dedicated servers. Open to learning if you haven't done it yet, but excited about it.

  • Game design instincts: the ability to look at one of our games and have informed opinions on what to build next, how to fit a feature to a specific genre or audience, and how to keep the experience cohesive as it grows.

  • Ability to speak Turkish (mother tongue of most members of the Publishing team).

Highlights

As part of our Publishing team, you'll take ownership of the games we own. You'll push regular updates, ship new content and features, and run live events.

About Zapata Quantum

Zapata Quantum is shaping the future of quantum computing: setting the standards for what’s viable, valuable, and worth building. The Company powers quantum applications across cryptography, pharmaceuticals, finance, materials discovery, defense, and beyond, translating cutting-edge research into real-world impact.

Zapata is the only organization to have contributed across every technical area of DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking program, giving it a uniquely comprehensive view of what it takes to make quantum computing work in practice. Now restructured and sharply focused, Zapata Quantum stands alone as the only publicly traded, pure-play quantum software company fully dedicated to unlocking quantum’s commercial potential.

We’re rebuilding at a pivotal moment for the industry—bringing together a team that will help define how quantum delivers value in the real world, with the opportunity for meaningful ownership as we shape the commercial path forward.

About the role

We are seeking a Quantum Fault-Tolerant Architecture Specialist to lead development of the software stack that maps logical quantum circuits to executable fault-tolerant implementations. You will own the architecture roadmap, compilation methodology, and physical resource-estimation models across different codes and architecture paradigms.

This high-ownership role sits at the boundary of quantum error correction, architecture, and software. You will define fault-tolerant semantics, reference implementations, error budgets, and validation criteria; guide a compiler engineer building production infrastructure; and partner with quantum algorithm scientists on key workloads. You will have access to advisors including Austin Fowler and Alexandru Paler, with opportunities to publish and contribute to open-source tools. This position is classified as exempt under applicable wage and hour laws.

What you'll do

  • Own the roadmap for translating logical circuits into fault-tolerant operations, layouts, schedules, and costed physical implementations
  • Develop code-aware lowering and resource models for surface, qLDPC, color, and emerging codes under explicit hardware, connectivity, and noise assumptions
  • Lead software components and APIs for code geometry, logical operations, syndrome extraction, decoding, routing, scheduling, and magic-state factories
  • Build reproducible estimators for physical qubits, runtime, space-time volume, throughput, failure probability, and uncertainty
  • Benchmark decoders, QEC simulations, logical error rates, and architecture tradeoffs
  • Define fault-tolerant IR constructs, backend passes, tests, and specifications with the compiler engineer on the team
  • Co-design resource estimates with algorithm scientists for cryptographic, chemistry, and simulation workloads
  • Track emerging codes, gates, decoders, and architectures; deliver recommendations through software, publications, technical reports, and program deliverables

Qualifications

  • PhD or equivalent in a related field, with research focused on quantum error correction or fault-tolerant quantum computing
  • Established record in code design, decoding, fault-tolerant logical operations, architecture, or compilation
  • Deep command of stabilizer and subsystem codes, syndrome extraction, logical errors, and code-family tradeoffs
  • Ability to derive physical qubit counts, runtime, and space-time volume from a logical workload and failure target
  • Hands-on Python and experience building research-quality QEC, compiler, simulation, or resource-estimation software
  • Experience evaluating decoders via Monte Carlo simulation, logical-error analysis, and extrapolation
  • Systems understanding of logical operations, feed-forward, routing, scheduling, magic-state supply, classical decoding, and hardware constraints
  • Ability to set a roadmap, expose assumptions, collaborate across disciplines, and communicate clearly

Preferred Experience

  • Substantive contributions to open-source QEC or fault-tolerant compilation tools such as tqec, Stim, Qualtran, Bench-Q, or comparable systems
  • Expertise beyond a single code family, especially qLDPC or color codes, code switching or gauge fixing, transversal gates, lattice surgery, or modular fault-tolerant architectures
  • Experience with hardware-aware QEC, real-time or accelerated decoding, and physical error models for superconducting, neutral-atom, trapped-ion, or photonic platforms
  • Familiarity with compiler IRs and verification techniques (for example QIR/MLIR, equivalence checking, property-based testing, SMT, Lean, or Coq)
  • Experience with government-funded research programs

Do you want to work for a mission-driven non-profit, writing software that will contribute to helping the livelihoods of millions of coffee farmers around the world? Enveritas is a 501(c)(3) non-profit and Y Combinator-backed startup looking to hire for our Engineering & Data Group. We are looking for a backend software engineer with a focus on python and PostgreSQL to join our EUDR engineering team on a remote/global, full-time basis. You can learn more about this job and our group at

We're a small team and every hire makes a large impact, so we're careful and thorough when it comes to hiring, but we are actively considering candidates and moving them through the process as quickly as we can.

About Our Engineering & Data Group

We are a quirky, talented, and humble group of about thirty people with diverse backgrounds, ranging from journalism to academia to international industry. We’re represented across the gender spectrum, with 36% of our Engineering and Data Group identifying as women and/or nonbinary. Several of us are parents, with more expecting.

Our group builds software to collect, analyze, and report data about coffee farmers’ conditions and practices. This large-scale data-collection effort requires many moving parts to work together, and we use technology to support that effort at every step of the process — from identifying coffee farms in satellite imagery, to coordinating survey edits across country teams, to detecting data anomalies in real-time that can be investigated while teams are still in the field. A core part of our work is in data aggregation and report generation, with insights ultimately being shared with roasters and other stakeholders on how to assist in improving the social, economic, and environmental conditions of smallholder farmers.

Our backend systems use Python and PostgreSQL/PostGIS, running in containerized services on AWS. We use GitHub and CI/CD, and Terraform for newer services.

What You’ll Be Doing

This role is part of our EUDR engineering team. Your work will focus on the backend systems that ingest customer-submitted farm lists, validate and transform those inputs, and run them against our deforestation detection model and geospatial datasets.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Backend feature development and maintenance. Implement improvements to our EUDR backend services, refine geospatial workflows, and strengthen data checks and error handling.
  • Investigative problem-solving. When something doesn’t look right to our Support team, you will help trace through data, assumptions, and system behavior to understand what happened and how to fix it.
  • Working with ambiguous or evolving requirements. EUDR is a regulated space where guidance changes, and internal requests are sometimes incomplete. You’ll help clarify what’s needed and translate it into practical engineering work.
  • Adapting the system to regulatory updates. As the EU releases new FAQs or adjustments, you will help interpret their implications and adapt parts of the system to remain consistent and compliant.
  • General backend engineering. Python + PostgreSQL/PostGIS development, improving observability, contributing to CI/CD pipelines, and helping make the system more resilient over time.

Although the role is primarily development-focused, you will also be responsible for applying and maintaining Terraform-based changes in AWS for the services you work on.

Qualifications

  • Strong ability to present and explain complex ideas clearly to non-technical colleagues.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply design patterns for creating modular and efficient software, with the ability to teach others how to solve architectural problems.
  • Extensive experience with Python, including developing applications and complex data processing tasks. Familiarity with Django or Flask.
  • Advanced experience with PostgreSQL, including query optimization, joins, stored procedures, and performance tuning.
  • Practical experience with Linux, Bash scripting, Docker containers, and AWS services (EC2, RDS, CloudFront).
  • A minimum of seven years of full-time professional experience as a backend software engineer.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent training in the principles of software engineering.

Research shows that people of different backgrounds read job postings differently. If you don’t think you meet all of the qualifications but do think you’d be a great match for us, please consider applying and sharing more in your application answers. We’d love to talk with you to see what skills you can bring to our team.

Who You Are

Our team is fully distributed, so you should be comfortable with remote work. This role is a full-time individual contributor role. While you can be located anywhere that our EOR (Deel) supports, our core hours are 10am to 2pm Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, with team members choosing either an early start or later stop as suits them.

You should be inspired by our mission to improve the lives of smallholder coffee farmers, and have an interest in sustainability. You should have a deep empathy for users of our tools and understand the importance of supporting the work of other teams. Because operational and business needs can be ambiguous and change on a short time-scale, you should have a love for environments with uncertainty, and enjoy not only solving problems, but discovering and demystifying them.

We are a small team! You should be comfortable working both independently and as a thoughtful collaborator, sensitive to the legibility and maintainability of your code when in the hands of your teammates.

About Working With Us & Compensation

Enveritas has teams around the world: we are about 150 people spread over more than two dozen countries, and of all backgrounds, faiths, and identities. To learn more about working at Enveritas, see

For a US-Based hire, base salary for this position will be between $135,000 and $155,000 annually (paid semi-monthly). This is a full-time exempt position. Full benefits include 401k with matching contributions, Medical/Dental/Vision, and Flexible Spending Account (FSA), 4 weeks vacation in addition to 13 standard holidays, and personal/sick time.

For a hire outside the US, our offer will be competitive; the specific benefits and compensation details will vary as required to account for your region’s laws and requirements. Salary for this position will be paid in relevant local currency.

Interview Process

We are committed to fair and equitable hiring. To honor this commitment, we are transparent about our interview process. See the hiring page at for details about our interview stages. After your introductory interview, we expect your interview process to take four to six weeks, consisting of four conversations that total about five hours of time. You should plan to also spend about four hours in total preparing for interviews.

How to Apply

Please apply using our Greenhouse application form. Feel free to contact us at should you have any questions about the position or the interview process. Questions about this opportunity or process will not reflect negatively on your application.

We care deeply about diversity. Our work is complex and nuanced, so the more diversity we have in the voices working on our problems, the larger of an impact our work can have for the world. We embrace and celebrate the unique experiences, perspectives, and cultural backgrounds that each individual brings to the workplace. We are dedicated to hiring employees who reflect the communities we serve and strongly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to apply.​

Also, Enveritas has been made aware of fake job postings by individuals pretending to hire persons seeking employment. jobs.excerpt: About Nebius:Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy.
jobs.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

Nebius Token Factory is building fast, reliable, and cost-efficient inference services for frontier models. As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on our Applied AI team, you will own model and endpoint optimization from model artifacts through production deployment. Your work will span model internals, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking, with a focus on improving latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while maintaining model quality and reliability.

This is a hands-on role in which you will work on complex optimization projects, diagnose difficult serving problems, and deliver measurable improvements in production. Working closely with kernel and platform engineers, you will evaluate serving configurations, resolve performance and quality regressions, and optimize inference for real-world workloads, supported by reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts.

Your responsibilities:

  • Own optimization work for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends.

  • Run engine comparisons and recommend practical serving configurations for specific workloads.

  • Debug model quality or performance regressions during production rollouts.

  • Optimize LLM and VLM endpoints for latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token.

  • Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend inference engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, or similar systems.

  • Build and productionize model-compression workflows, including quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery.

  • Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving.

  • Build reproducible benchmark harnesses for TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token.

  • Partner with GPU kernel engineers and platform engineers to diagnose bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers.

  • Write clear design docs, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.

Must-haves:

  • Strong Python and PyTorch engineering skills.

  • Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference systems.

  • Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or equivalent internal systems.

  • Strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks, including KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving.

  • Ability to reason quantitatively about latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost tradeoffs.

  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ, SmoothQuant, or related techniques.

  • Experience with distillation, speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa, multi-token prediction, or other inference acceleration methods.

  • Experience with agentic workloads, including tool calling, structured outputs, streaming APIs, high concurrency, and multi-step orchestration.

  • CUDA or Triton familiarity, even if the role is not primarily a kernel-engineering role.

  • Open-source contributions to vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer, LMCache, PyTorch, Triton, Ray, KServe, or related projects.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

jobs.description:
About Imagine Worldwide

All children have immense potential, but hundreds of millions don’t have access to the learning they need. Imagine Worldwide believes that every child should be empowered with the basic right to literacy and numeracy. We provide an innovative education technology solution and implementation model to the global literacy/numeracy learning crisis using the onebillion application and various toolkits and systems to support implementation. Our model is massively scalable, evidence-based, and can deliver foundational learning to millions of the most marginalized children.

Imagine Worldwide partners with governments, organizations, and communities to provide child-directed, tablet-based learning that is accessible, effective, and affordable. We are incorporated in California (United States) as a nonprofit organization, but operate in Sub-Saharan Africa through locally-registered entities in Malawi, Sierra Leone, and Tanzania. Learn more on our website.

Role Overview

The Senior Analytics Engineer builds, runs and improves Imagine’s analytics platform: the infrastructure, pipelines and core data models that the organisation’s reporting and analysis depend on. The central task is to scale the platform as data volumes grow, keeping costs under control without giving up performance. In a small team, that means covering the infrastructure underneath the data as well as the data engineering itself.

Imagine’s data comes from many sources. The largest is tablets in more than 1,500 schools across Malawi, Tanzania and Sierra Leone, which record learning activity as individual events, adding up to billions of records. These only become meaningful when joined with programme context, such as active schools per term, device allocations and enrolment, and with operational data from inventory and field data collection. Turning all of this into reliable data on a non-profit budget calls for careful decisions about where processing happens and what each workload costs.

The role reports to the Director of Analytics, who sets the platform’s architecture and technical standards, and works alongside the rest of the Analytics Team. We are looking for someone senior who takes initiative, turns architectural direction into working systems, and brings forward evidence-based proposals for improving them. As the engineer builds context, they take on increasing ownership of the platform’s day-to-day running and technical decisions.

Key Responsibilities

The Senior Analytics Engineer’s responsibilities fall into four pillars. The first two cover the platform itself: the infrastructure it runs on, and the pipelines that bring data in from many sources and process it at scale. The third covers orchestration and the core data models that the rest of the Analytics Team builds on. The fourth covers the practices that keep the platform reliable, secure and affordable to run.

Data Platform and Infrastructure

Imagine’s analytics platform runs on AWS and ClickHouse Cloud, with infrastructure managed as code. In a small team, this role carries the infrastructure work that a larger organisation would split across dedicated platform or DevOps staff, limited to the scope of the analytics platform.

  • Build and maintain the platform’s AWS infrastructure, including storage, compute, networking, the data catalogue, secrets and access management (S3, EC2, Glue Data Catalog, Lake Formation, IAM, Secrets Manager).
  • Manage infrastructure as code in Terraform, keeping environments reproducible, version-controlled and reviewable.
  • Administer the ClickHouse Cloud warehouse, including service configuration, user and role management, and monitoring of performance and capacity.
  • Host and maintain the team’s self-hosted tools, including Apache Superset for BI and Apache Airflow for orchestration. This covers deployment, upgrades, authentication and availability. The Senior BI & Data Analyst manages the dashboards and content within Superset.
  • Contribute to architectural decisions on how the platform evolves, setting out options and trade-offs for review with the Director of Analytics.

Large-Scale Data Processing and Pipelines

Data reaches the platform from application databases, operational systems and field data tools, and lands in an Apache Iceberg data lake on S3. Spark-based processing on AWS Glue does the heavy work before the data moves into ClickHouse for analysis. The aim is to do expensive processing once, as far upstream as practical, so that downstream models and queries stay fast and affordable.

  • Build and maintain ingestion pipelines from the platform’s sources, including application databases, APIs and operational systems, using tools such as AWS Glue, Airbyte and AWS Lambda.
  • Implement incremental loading patterns that stay efficient and recoverable as volumes grow, landing raw data in the lake in a form that preserves its full history.
  • Develop and optimise Spark jobs that process billions of device events into learning sessions and higher-level aggregates, paying close attention to partitioning, skew and compute cost.
  • Bring in and model the programme context that gives event data its meaning, such as schools, terms, device allocations and enrolment, and handle how that context changes over time.
  • Design and maintain Iceberg tables for performance and cost, including partitioning strategy, file sizing, compaction and snapshot management.
  • Validate data at ingestion and surface quality issues early, working with the Analytics Team to trace them back to their source.
  • Contribute to evaluating new processing approaches as volumes grow, including moving more work upstream and assessing where streaming would add value.

Orchestration and Transformation

Apache Airflow orchestrates the platform’s pipelines, and dbt transforms data in ClickHouse into the models that reporting and analysis rely on. This role builds and maintains the foundational layers of those models.

  • Build and maintain Airflow workflows that coordinate ingestion, processing and transformation, with clear dependencies, retries and alerting.
  • Develop and maintain dbt staging and core models in ClickHouse, following consistent conventions for naming, structure and materialisation.
  • Implement incremental models for high-volume tables, choosing materialisation strategies and table designs that balance freshness, correctness and cost.
  • Write and maintain dbt tests and model contracts for core datasets, so that changes that would break downstream reporting are caught before they reach production.
  • Document core models such as learning sessions as agreed definitions, including their lineage, and make clear where a model applies an approximation rather than a direct transformation.
  • Work with the Senior BI & Data Analyst on the boundary between core and reporting models, and with the Data Scientist on datasets for research and evaluation.

Reliability, Cost and Engineering Practice

A small team needs a platform that runs predictably and that more than one person understands. This pillar covers the engineering practices that make that possible.

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions for infrastructure, pipeline and dbt code, including automated checks that stop unsafe changes from reaching production.
  • Implement monitoring and alerting across pipelines, the warehouse and hosted tools, so that failures and delays are visible quickly and reach the right people.
  • Respond to platform incidents and data issues, carry out root cause analysis, and contribute to the team’s data quality incident process.
  • Apply and maintain access controls and security practices across the data lake, warehouse and BI layer, in line with Imagine’s data governance policies.
  • Monitor platform costs across AWS and ClickHouse, track the cost and performance of individual workloads over time, and use that evidence to identify savings and prioritise optimisation work.
  • Maintain and periodically test backup and recovery procedures for the platform’s core components.
  • Take part in code review and write clear runbooks and technical documentation, following the team’s documentation standards, so that knowledge of the platform is shared across the team.

Requirements

The qualifications below are grouped by importance. Core requirements are needed to do the role from the start. Strongly preferred skills shorten the time it takes to become effective on Imagine’s platform. Advantageous experience adds value but is not expected. We do not expect any one candidate to bring everything listed here.

Education

  • A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Demonstrated experience is weighted equally to formal credentials.

Experience

  • At least 7 years in data engineering, software engineering or platform engineering roles, including at least 3 years building and running distributed data processing (Spark or equivalent) in production.
  • A track record of taking responsibility for a production data platform, or major parts of one, including its reliability, performance and day-to-day operation.
  • Experience working with datasets in the hundreds of millions to billions of records, and designing processing that stays efficient as volumes grow.
  • Experience running data workloads within real budget constraints: making deliberate trade-offs between compute, storage and performance, and being able to show the effect of those decisions.
  • Experience managing the cloud infrastructure that data workloads run on, not only using managed services.
  • Experience in small teams where engineers cover a broad scope and work with limited supervision.
  • Experience working with remote teams across multiple countries and time zones.
  • Experience in the non-profit, international development or social sector is an advantage but not a requirement.

Technical Skills: Core

  • Strong Python, written to production standards, with testing and modular design.
  • Advanced SQL, including writing and optimising queries against analytical databases.
  • Spark (PySpark), including performance tuning for partitioning, shuffles and data skew.
  • A solid understanding of data lake design, including columnar formats such as Parquet, partitioning strategy, and when to process in the lake rather than the warehouse.
  • Hands-on AWS experience with data services and the infrastructure around them, such as S3, Glue or EMR, IAM and EC2.
  • Infrastructure as code, using Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK or similar.
  • Linux administration and Docker, to the level needed to deploy and maintain self-hosted services.
  • dbt in production, including incremental models and testing.
  • Workflow orchestration with Airflow, Dagster, Prefect or similar.
  • Git, CI/CD and code review practice.

Technical Skills: Strongly Preferred

  • Apache Iceberg, or another open table format such as Delta Lake or Hudi.
  • ClickHouse, or a comparable columnar warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift.
  • Terraform specifically.
  • Apache Airflow specifically.
  • AWS Glue and Lake Formation.
  • Data modelling for analytics, including handling reference data that changes over time.

Technical Skills: Advantageous

  • Managed Spark platforms such as Databricks.
  • Streaming technologies such as Kafka, Flink, Kinesis or Spark Structured Streaming.
  • Event, telemetry or IoT data, particularly from devices that sync intermittently.
  • Ingestion tools such as Airbyte.
  • Administering BI tools such as Apache Superset.
  • Software development beyond data pipelines, such as building APIs or system integrations.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience.

Location

The Senior Analytics Engineer must be based in Africa. The role will frequently collaborate and coordinate with operations teams across Africa, the US, and the UK.

This is a full-time remote position; the role can be based anywhere in Africa with reliable internet access and alignment with core working hours across time zones. The role may involve occasional international travel for in-person team meetings, field support or training, as needed. Candidates should be comfortable working independently in a virtual environment and coordinating with colleagues across global teams.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis

Join Our Vision: We are building the next generation of Spatial Media - a new way people experience videos through interaction, multi-user presence, haptics, AI, and immersive storytelling.

DeoVR is the leading immersive streaming technology serving multiple enterprise customers and millions of users globally.

We are now expanding the boundaries of what video can be - moving from passive watching to active, interactive, multi-user journeys.

If this excites you more than it scares you, you are in the right place.

The Role

We are looking for a Compositing Artist (Project-Based) to deliver clean, high-quality composites that meet the technical and visual demands of immersive media production.

This role is not about "removing backgrounds" - it is about precision craft: extracting clean keys from complex footage, preserving fine detail, and delivering master-ready files that hold up in immersiveenvironments where every edge matters.

What You Will Do

  • Extract clean, high-quality keys from green screen footage, including challenging cases involving hair, motion blur, and mixed lighting conditions

  • Perform spill suppression, edge refinement, and matte cleanup to create seamless final composites

  • Deliver clean alpha channels and production-ready assets in agreed formats

  • Prepare master projects and render high-quality master files optimized for streaming platforms

What We Are Looking For

  • Proven experience in compositing and green screen post-production workflows

  • Strong understanding of keying, alpha channels, spill suppression, edge treatment, and matte generation

  • Proficiency in DaVinci Resolve Fusion

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering high-quality visual results

  • Fluency in English (B2+)

Bonus Points

  • Experience working with VR, 180°, or 360° video content

Hiring Process

  • HR Screening (30 min)

  • Team Interview (up to 1 hour)

  • Case Task (2-4 hours)

  • CEO Interview (30 min)

💼Explore our hiring process

What We Offer

Please note, that this is a fully remote contract role. B2B cooperation only – you will work with us as an independent contractor operating through your own legal business entity (e.g., sole proprietorship, limited company, or equivalent).

  • The chance to be part of a pioneering team in a rapidly evolving industry

  • Direct impact on the future of immersive media

  • Flexible working hours and remote-first culture

  • A team that values initiative, clarity, and collaboration

  • Access to all tools and tech you need

  • Unlimited DeoVR Premium

  • A work environment where ideas matter and people are treated with respect

Stay Connected

Join our Facebook community and follow updates as we advance interactive VR experiences through cutting-edge technology. Join us and step into a role where legal expertise meets innovation.

jobs.description:
Art Director

Heptic Arena — Full-Time — Remote (Europe)

About Prism Studio

Prism Studio is a Malta-based game development studio building unforgettable, player-first experiences with bold ideas and cutting-edge design. We're a small, cross-disciplined team, self-managing from wherever in the world we happen to be, united by a shared goal: making games we'd want to play ourselves. Heptic Arena, is a PvPvE multiplayer showdown shooter that is heading to Steam Early Access and the Epic Games Store, and it's built entirely in Unreal Engine.

About the Role

We're looking for an experienced Art Director with a strong background in art content production to lead the artistic vision and visual communication of Heptic Arena. You'll own every aspect of art content development, from first concepts to release ready assets (characters, species design, arena environments, weapons, UI/UX, concept art, and all player facing visuals) Working closely with creative leadership and cross-functional teams to keep the game cohesive, visually striking, and true to Heptic Arena's world.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll set the artistic vision, direct a talented art team, and stay closely involved in production, from early concepts through to live content updates after release.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the art direction of Heptic Arena across environment art, character/species art, animation, modelling, rigging, texturing, shader development, concept art, 2D, and UI/UX, setting clear direction so every asset is consistent, high-quality, and true to the game's identity.
  • Keep the species roster and world cohesive: maintain a consistent visual language across playable species (and future roster additions, skins, and cosmetics) as the game grows through Early Access and beyond.
  • Partner with creative and Technical Leadership: collaborate closely with the Creative Director, Game Designers, Technical Leaders, and PO to keep gameplay, design, and art seamlessly integrated across a live PvPvE arena shooter.
  • Build and maintain 3D art pipelines in Unreal Engine, solving technical challenges with cross-functional teams and optimizing workflows to support both quality and the pace of live-service content, new arenas, seasonal content, and post-launch drops.
  • Track progress and keep the team aligned using tools such as Jira and Confluence, monitoring milestones and giving regular feedback so the Art team stays on schedule without compromising quality.Initiate, plan, execute and control art content development.

About You

  • Bachelor's degree in Art, Design, or a closely related discipline. This academic foundation is expected to be complemented by substantial professional experience in a production environment.
  • A minimum of seven years of professional experience within the gaming industry is required. Exposed to the full lifecycle of game development, from pre-production through to live operations.
  • Must have hands-on experience delivering stylized games that rely on hand-painted textures. Skilled in maintaining a distinctive and cohesive visual identity across a roster of characters and environments.
  • At least one AA or AAA title must have been shipped under the candidate's direction or direct contribution. Must have knowledge and ability to see a large-scale production through to release.
  • Have a strong portfolio spanning traditional art skills, 3D art, animation, UI, and concept art. The portfolio should reflect versatility across disciplines as well as a consistently high standard of craftsmanship.
  • Excellent managerial and communication skills are required to lead and manage all of the art disciplines (2D, 3D, animation,...) within an agile production framework. The successful candidate will use tools such as Jira and Confluence to monitor milestones and provide regular feedback. Experience in Jira Advanced Roadmaps or Jira Plans will be considered a big plus.
  • Demonstrated experience resolving technical challenges in collaboration with cross-functional teams is essential. Must be able to optimize production workflows and improve both efficiency and creative output,
  • Proficiency in Maya and Substance Painter is required for this role.
  • Excellent communication, leadership, and management skills are essential to this role. These qualities should be evidenced through hands-on production experience, ideally within a distributed or globally remote team.

Life at Prism Studio

We work as one unit with one common goal. Our purpose is to build a cross-disciplined team where everyone is self-managing, wherever they are in the world. We collaborate in an open, friendly way, as a global team built on talent and communication.
